newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU set to adopt grain export tenders - officials.
newsitem.headline: EU set to adopt grain export tenders - officials.

text.p: The European Union is set to adopt on Thursday regulations allowing its suspended tenders for grain export subsidies to start working again by the end of the month, member country officials said.
The measures being adopted shortly at a cereals management committee in Brussels will open export tenders for wheat, barley and rye from the open market in the 1997/98 season (July/June).
They will come into force at the first cereals management meeting to be held after publication in the EU's Journal, and bidding will in any event start by the end of the month, the officials said.

One question mark remained over the timing of export tenders for oats, amid legal debate over whether to continue a two-year transitional arrangement for Finland and Sweden. Officials stressed that oats exports, mainly to the U.S., would be opened, perhaps soon, but legal work remained to be completed.
Another said oats exports were unlikely to be opened before August for what is a slightly late-sown crop this year.
The opening of tenders, described as "likely" when the meeting's agenda was circulated on Tuesday, did not necessarily mean exports would resume at once, officials said.
